title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning.
author: Weihao Cheng

title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent
summary: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch.
author: Yuxin Jiang, Wenqiang Sun, Jiaqi Li, et al.

title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
summary: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed.
author: Amine Lbath, Manan Suri, Aurelien Delaitre, et al.

title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
summary: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget.
author: Yang Meng, Zixin Ding, Robert L. Grossman, et al.

title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model.
author: Kai Lu, Chenyang Ma, Ioannis Havoutis

title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under
summary: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality.
author: Terence D. Agbeyegbe, Toneukarin G. Agbeyegbe

title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes.
author: Jiahao Huang, Jun Wang

title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM
summary: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches.
author: Ana E. Sanchez Villalobos, Michael D. Quinn, Aakash Tyagi, et al.

title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
summary: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers.
author: Adrià Ciurana Lanau, Harleen Hanspal, Lusine Abrahamyan, et al.

title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
summary: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients.
author: Sean Tang, Peiran Wang, Ying Li, et al.

title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using

author: Amirali Khosravi, Jaidip M. Jagtap, D. Chamil Codipilly, et al.

title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
summary: When multimodal decision models determine actions, moderation outcomes, or quality judgments, their reliability depends on preserving semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignoring irrelevant additions, and distinguishing information consistent with task evidence from information that conflicts with it.
author: Jinzhe Li, Qi Wang, Dandan Guo, et al.

title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
summary: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. author: Md. Abdullah Al Zami, Suraiya Shanaz, Mahdi Hasan, et al.

title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
summary: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal
author: Nathaniel Cohen, Nicolas Dufour, Amélie Royer, et al.

title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
summary: Intersectional bias arises when a model treats people who hold several marginalised identities at once differently from what their separate identities would predict. Auditing such intersectional subgroups remains a challenge: their number grows quadratically, and there is no agreed baseline for what independent
author: George Rahul, Ronit Jahilal, Bhaskara Hanuma Vedula, et al.

title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
summary: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents
summary: Agent applications are increasingly deployed, yet agent-specific attacks pose real threats to them. Upon a security incident, organizations backtrack to identify the CEP (compromise entry point), remediate the damage, and prevent its recurrence.
author: Yicheng Cai, Taegyu Kim, Peng Liu

title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers
summary: Decision models enable fast, confidence-aware decisions by scoring candidate answers in a single forward pass, without generating text or intermediate reasoning. Yet reasoning can substantially improve decision quality, raising the question of whether its benefits can be retained without the cost of generating it.
author: Sahibzada Allahyar, Julia White, Dhruv Atreja, et al.

title: FLUID: Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance
summary: Real-time task guidance is inherently flexible: when an agent guides a user through a task, multiple responses and timings can be appropriate, and sometimes the best action is to remain silent.
author: Yunqi Zhao, Run Peng, Ze Dong, et al.

title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
summary: We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives.
author: Francesco Caporali, Jason M. Altschuler, Boris Hanin

title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces
summary: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next. author: Andrew Kang

title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
summary: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action
summary: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback.
author: Yuzhi Huang, Jie Wu, Fanding Huang, et al.

title: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining
summary: Frontier text-to-image (T2I) foundation models predominantly rely on multi-billion parameter Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) pretrained across massive compute clusters, creating an accessibility barrier for academic laboratories.
author: Víctor Rodrigo González, Pablo M. Olmos, Ignacio Peis, et al.

title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives.
author: Yiyang Du, Yuxuan Kuang, Qitao Zhao, et al.

title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
summary: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions.
author: Jochen Laubrock

title: Hybrid Retrieval for Government Scheme Search in English and Marathi

title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
summary: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification.
author: Guoxin Chen, Shuang Sun, Fanzhe Meng, et al.

title: Multimodal Error Detection in Chest X-ray Reports: A Large Language Model Reading Image
summary: Rad-Linter checks chest X-ray reports against image-derived evidence to flag potential errors for review. A pretrained image classifier supplies scores for nine pathologies, and a 1.5B-parameter language model, fine-tuned with LoRA on 1,816 examples, checks their consistency with the report.
author: Yanda Cheng, Bo Wen, Yuhao Lu

title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management
summary: Long-term agents accumulate large external memory stores as interactions unfold, increasing the costs of storage, retrieval, and response generation. title: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate
summary: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. However, this knowledge is typically scattered across projects and document structures, making it difficult to locate relevant, contextual information when making decisions.
author: Oriol Alàs, Ian Palacín, Iván Cester, et al.

title: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs
summary: Attention in large language models (LLMs) scores every query against every key with a full dot product. We investigate whether this dot product must be computed completely for attention to be effective.
author: Ambroise Borbely, Mathieu Salzmann, Olivier Verscheure

title: Beam Model Technical Report
summary: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters, specifically built and optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam delivers frontier level reasoning, while requiring 3-4x less inference compute than many models of its class.
author: Reflection Team, Adam Abdulhamid, Osama Abuelsorour, et al.

title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination
summary: Hallucination research in low-resource languages fragments easily: each newly named failure mode prompts its own dataset, spending scarce annotators on incomparable resources. We argue for consolidation and test it at community scale.
author: Asif Shahriyar Sushmit, Shefayat E Shams Adib, Abdullah Al Jubaer Gem, et al.

title: Language-Oriented Semantic Modeling for Target Language Extraction
summary: Target Language Extraction (TLE) aims to isolate speech in a target language from multilingual mixtures. Existing approaches primarily rely on acoustic modeling with language identity labels, which provide only coarse categorical guidance.
author: Mehmet Sinan Yıldırım, Ke Zhang, Shuai Wang, et al.

title: BADAS-3.0: Real-Time Driving Perception and Planning from One Camera
summary: We ask how far a driving model can get with one camera and real-time latency. BADAS-3.0 is a 1B-parameter video encoder with four small heads. author: Roni Goldshmidt, Hamish Scott, Lorenzo Niccolini

summary: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews. At ICLR, measured overlap rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, in reviews from the same stage of the review process, with year-on-year rises at NeurIPS, ICML and the F1000 and PLOS
author: Ilya Gusev

title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?
summary: Reasoning capabilities in large language models have evolved from prompting-based methods to internalized model behaviors. In this paper, we investigate whether the internal thinking model of an LLM can be deliberately changed and whether such a change is beneficial.
author: Marc Jansen

title: dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement
summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) support parallel generation, yet they often require many denoising steps because only a fraction of token predictions are sufficiently reliable to be committed at each step. Existing acceleration methods primarily optimize confidence learning or commitment policies.
author: Handa Li, Pengxiang Li, Mingyu Cao, et al.

title: STAGE: Spatio-Temporal Augmented Graph Expansion for Weakly Supervised Cross-Tweet Event
summary: Causal relations in disaster-related social media of- ten span independent posts, making cross-tweet causal discovery difficult to supervise and model at scale. We propose STAGE, a framework that separates scalable cross-tweet weak-supervision construction from spatio-temporal relational learning over event
author: Hieu Minh Duong, Todd Gary, Eugene Levin, et al.

title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
summary: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments.
author: Yang Wan, Linchao Zhu

title: Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author
summary: Given a single text and a simple zero-shot prompt (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer "who wrote this?" at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who.
author: Atrey Desai, Deniz Böloni-Turgut, Ty Brassington, et al.

title: Learning to Think with Images Faithfully via Adaptive Data Selection
summary: Thinking with images (TwI) empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to overcome perceptual bottlenecks by actively cropping and zooming into fine-grained visual details, promising both higher accuracy and interpretable, region-grounded reasoning.
author: Yu Zhao, Jiaxin Zhang, Rohit Saxena, et al.

title: Can World Models Predict Rice Growth? Toward Agricultural World Models
summary: World models can imagine how a physical scene evolves over the next few seconds, but growers need to know how a crop will develop over weeks to months: will this rice plant have headed a month from now, and how will it look at harvest?
author: Wenkai Ji, Zeteng Li, Yinkun Guo, et al.

title: RL Can Only Reinforce What It Sees Succeed
summary: When a familiar rule stops working, an agent has to weigh what pre-training taught it against what it now observes. author: Ruben Sanchez-Corcuera, Unai Zulaika, Aritz Bilbao-Jayo, et al.

title: Same Judgement, Different Scores: Numerical Scoring Topology in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
summary: LLMs are increasingly used as automated evaluators to reduce the cost and time required for human annotation. However, the role of scoring-scheme design in the reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation remains underexplored.
author: Doyun Kim, Chanwoo Kim, Jiwoo Kum, et al.

title: Understanding MoE Decisions Beyond Gradients
summary: Understanding a language model's decision requires knowing how its internal computations affect its preference between answers. Gradient-based methods estimate this influence by predicting the effect of changing those computations.
author: Zhen Xu, Zitao Zhang, Kevin Zhao, et al.

title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the

title: SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents
summary: Spreadsheets are widely used for data analysis and supporting decision-making. Automating spreadsheet analysis while protecting sensitive data and controlling deployment costs motivates locally deployed open-weight large language models (LLMs).
author: Yuxiang Wang, Junhao Gan, Jianzhong Qi

summary: Backpropagation remains the dominant method for training deep neural networks, but its reliance on non-local computations has motivated the search for biologically plausible alternatives.

title: Revealing Pathway Interactions in Network Computations with Complete Path Contribution
summary: Networks pass signals through many layers of interconnected units, so explaining what they compute means tracing how information travels from input to output and how pathways interact. Most existing approaches analyze only pairwise interactions between components such as units, layers or attention heads.

summary: When should a deployed MI decoder spend adaptation resources-not only how to adapt under shift? summary: Worldwide, people produce and listen to music to induce, express, and regulate their own and others' emotions. To what extent culture influences the emotions evoked by music is, however, contested.

summary: The neuromuscular junction represents a relevant experimental model for revealing important biophysical mechanisms underlying synaptic transmission. summary: Human vision and video stereo networks both reuse disparity evidence across time, yet a refresh of the input can invalidate a match formed milliseconds earlier. What tells a system whether an old match still counts? We answer this from limited human data in three steps.

summary: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories?

summary: This paper presents a novel methodological framework, integrating a dual self-organising map (SOM) neural network architecture with Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), for assessing instructional efficiency within learning environments.

summary: Animals generate behavior through continuous interactions between their neural circuits, bodies, and environment. Embodied simulations study these interactions by testing neural circuit models in biologically realistic settings.

summary: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging.

summary: Magnetoreception has been primarily studied in orientation and navigation, but whether Earth-strength magnetic fields influence non-spatial decisions remains unclear. Evidence for human magnetic responses is limited, and the transduction mechanism is unknown.

title: Near Resonance, Less Ordered: Radius and Mass Ordering in Compact Multi-planet Systems
summary: Compact multi-planet systems exhibit a tendency for planetary radii to follow ordered sequences with orbital position, suggesting that these non-random patterns preserve a fossil record of their formation.
author: Agustin Heron, Songhu Wang, Cristobal Petrovich

title: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
summary: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties.
author: Luke Keyte, Thomas J. Haworth, Tyger Peake, et al.

title: A novel method for dust evolution in protoplanetary disks and a new criterion for gap opening
summary: We present the Grain Residence-Time Method (GRTM), a computationally efficient particle-tracking approach for studying dust evolution and trapping in protoplanetary disks. By reconstructing steady-state dust distributions from particle residence times, this method provides a way to obtain radial dust surface density
author: SM Gopika, Paul C. Duffell

title: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of
summary: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. title: Planet Formation in a Warped Disc: Gravitational Instability and Misaligned Infall
summary: We perform three-dimensional smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations to investigate the impact of misaligned infall on a gravitationally unstable protoplanetary disc. The interaction between the disc and the infalling gas does not occur uniformly across all radii.
author: Sahl Rowther, Josh Calcino, Richard Alexander

title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
summary: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone.
author: Omoruyi Atekha, Marcus Greiff, Ray Zhang, et al.

title: Susceptibility source separation via Closed-form Alternating Newton-type Optimization
summary: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM) provides a bulk magnetic susceptibility estimate per voxel, so contributions from paramagnetic and diamagnetic sources within the same voxel partially cancel.
author: Ignacio Contreras-Zúñiga, Cristian Tejos, Carlos Milovic

title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias
summary: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits.
author: Roi Yozevitch, Shmuel Sternklar, Ziv Glasser

title: Deterministic Temporal Embedding for Calcium Imaging Trace Extraction
summary: Reliable extraction of calcium-dependent fluorescence traces in calcium imaging sequences requires identifying pixels whose fluorescence intensity reflects the same underlying cellular activity.
author: Qi Gao, Julius Beichert, Miriam Ratliff, et al.

title: OffBeat: Multicoset Sampling for 4D Capture Beyond the Camera Frame Rate
summary: For 4D reconstruction, a synchronized multi-camera rig records all views at the same timestamps and misses the motion between them. Staggered triggers spread the same frames over more timestamps.
author: Chi-Wei Lee, An-Kai Chen, Cheng-Han Chiang, et al.

title: FirstCross: Convex Single-Photon 3D Reconstruction from Sparse Views
summary: Single-photon lidar records the arrival time of each returning photon, enabling 3D reconstruction from few views and scarce photons. However, leading neural methods such as Transientangelo require over an hour of non-convex per-scene optimization, and their accuracy degrades as photon flux decreases.
author: Chi-Wei Lee, Cheng-Han Chiang, Yi-Chun Chang, et al.

title: MambaLIFT: Reference-Based Mechanism-Aware Attribution for VMamba
summary: Attributing predictions of visual state-space models remains challenging because input-dependent selective dynamics couple feature selection, recurrent state propagation, and shared computational pathways.
author: Jintu Kakati, Niladri B. Puhan

title: Passing NPCR Without Diffusion: Exact Signatures, a Detection Benchmark and an Audit of
summary: NPCR, the share of ciphertext bytes changed by a one-pixel plaintext change, is reported for nearly every image cipher as evidence of diffusion, with 99.61% the target. Several mechanisms produce values near it, and the mean does not say which.
author: Mua'ad Alfarajat

title: LBW-NPS: A Local Band-Weighted Noise Power Spectrum Loss for Texture-Preserving Low-Dose CT
summary: Low-dose CT denoising should suppress noise while retaining the local texture of the reference image. Matching a pooled spectrum can overlook regional discrepancies, whereas pixel losses alone can favor overly smooth outputs.
author: Fatma Elif Yalçındağ, Mehmet Ozan Ünal, Metin Ertaş, et al.

title: Life-IQA+: Boosting Blind Image Quality Assessment via GCN-enhanced Layer Interaction and
summary: Blind image quality assessment (BIQA) is essential for evaluating and optimizing visual experience. Existing BIQA methods typically aggregate features from multiple backbone stages without accounting for their unequal contributions to quality prediction.
author: Long Tang, Guoquan Zheng, Huiyu Duan, et al.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning for Prediction of Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in
summary: To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-aware multimodal learning framework for predicting radiation-induced xerostomia in patients receiving head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy. We developed a Bidirectional Attention-enhanced Diffusion Transformer (BA-DiT) that combines self-supervised multimodal representation learning
author: Jin Yang, Tian Liu, Jose Penagaricano, et al.

title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense
summary: BraTS-GoAT Task 3 evaluates brain-tumor segmentation across heterogeneous entities using shared ET, TC, and WT regions. We present a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels, a training-only nested-region objective, and a four-expert bottleneck adapter.
author: Heeseung Shin, Changwon Lim

title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation
summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) is increasingly applied to scientific imaging domains, such as microscopy, where labels are scarce but noisy data is abundant. These domains exhibit significant signal-dependent noise, which can create a representational shortcut: since both augmented views derive from the same noisy
author: Oankar R. Patil, May D. Wang

title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly
summary: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality.
author: Ioana-Sabina Stoian, Florinel-Alin Croitoru, Vlad Hondru, et al.

title: Transferable Named Sparse Features for Morphology-based Gleason Grading
summary: Deep learning systems grade prostate biopsies at the level of pathologists, but most report a grade without the glandular architecture that justifies it. This work presents a grading system built on a sparse code over the tokens of a pathology foundation model.
author: Argyrios Zafeiriou, Athanasios Kallipolitis, Ilias Maglogiannis

title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering
summary: Images often require both denoising and interpolation, yet treating the two tasks separately is suboptimal: interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates subsequent denoising, while denoising may remove image details useful for interpolation.
author: Gene Cheung, Niruhan Viswarupan, Romisaa Elsaidy

title: Stochastic Optimisation for Scalable Ptychographic Image Reconstruction
summary: X-ray ptychography is a lensless coherent diffraction imaging technique capable of high spatial resolution, in which an image is reconstructed by solving a large-scale inverse problem from highly redundant far-field diffraction measurements acquired under overlapping illumination.
author: Alan W. Muriithi, Jared Tanner, Jaroslav M. Fowkes, et al.

title: Micrograph B-factor estimation via Wilson statistics
summary: The single-particle cryo-electron microscopy imaging process is known to cause exponential decay in the amplitude and power spectra of proteins. This decay is modeled by the B factor and is currently corrected as a post-processing stage of the 3D reconstruction.
author: Ayelet Heimowitz, Amit Singer

title: Gaussian Splatoms: Direct Atomic Structure Identification in Electron Tomography
summary: Atomic electron tomography (AET) computationally reconstructs the 3D atomic structure of materials from a series of 2D projection measurements acquired at different tilt angles. Inspired by Gaussian splatting techniques from computer vision, we introduce an atom-centric parameterization for modeling AET samples.
author: Nalini Singh, Tiffany Chien, Cedric Lim, et al.

title: LIC-Audit: How Comparable Are Reported Gains in Learned Image Compression?
summary: Learned image compression (LIC) papers often report BD-rate improvements of only a few percent. They are measured against VTM reference software whose version keeps changing: the claims we audit name 7 versions, 5 in 2025 papers alone.
author: Haisheng Fu, Jie Liang, Runyu Yang, et al.

title: Uncovering the Invisible in Routine Radiology: Cross-Modal Detection of MRI-Verified
summary: Routine X-ray modalities like cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) are optimized for high-contrast mineralized tissues, leaving soft-tissue abnormalities buried beneath photon noise and below human visual perception. Thus, detecting non-calcified pathologies requires secondary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
author: Evgeny Alves Limarenko

title: Streaming Generative Video Compression with Embedding Alignment and In-Context Propagation
summary: Video compression at ultra-low bitrates presents substantial challenges in preserving perceptual quality. Although pretrained video diffusion transformers (DiTs) provide powerful generative priors, existing generative video compression (GVC) methods built on them typically rely on computationally expensive VAE
author: Zhitao Wang, Hengyu Man, Han Liu, et al.

title: SWIMSS: An Open Multi-Center SwinUNETR Model for Multiple Sclerosis White Matter Lesion
summary: Purpose: To develop and validate SWIMSS (SWInUNETR for Multiple Sclerosis white matter lesion Segmentation), a SwinUNETR-based deep learning (DL) model for reliable automated white matter (WM) lesion segmentation, in a large multicentric cohort of people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS).
author: Federico Spagnolo, Po-Jui Lu, Mario Ocampo-Pineda, et al.

title: SurgCBVR: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Content-Based Surgical Video-to-Video Retrieval
summary: Hospitals record thousands of hours of surgical video annually, yet these archives remain difficult to search by content. Surgeons cannot readily retrieve similar operations, complications, or workflow events. Existing surgical computer vision primarily produces labels rather than retrieving relevant videos.
author: Mohammad Eslami, Mousa Moradi, Negin Ghamsarian, et al.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Benchmarking Uncertainty Quantification in Retinal Disease Screening
summary: Reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for evaluating retinal AI systems beyond classification accuracy, yet it remains unclear whether existing UQ strategies generalize across diseases, model architectures, and reliability criteria.
author: Mahvash Jebeli, Mohammad Eslami, Nazlee Zebardast, et al.

title: Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity
summary: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is at the center of modern machine learning and is known to be statistically minimax-optimal in many regression settings, e.g., for convex Generalized Linear Models (GLMs).
author: Valentin Roth, Marco Avella Medina

title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
summary: In real-world black-box optimization problems, a mechanistic simulator is often available that approximately predicts the behavior of the system as a function of the parameters being optimized.
author: Tristan Fauvel, Federico Pavone, Titouan Guillou, et al.

title: Exact Bayesian layers via characteristic functions

title: Statistical Inference with Ill-Conditioned Random Weight Neural Network Sieves
summary: Random weight neural networks (RWNNs) are shallow networks whose hidden-layer parameters are randomly generated and then kept fixed, while only the output coefficients are estimated. Conditional on the sampled parameters, RWNN regression is a linear sieve problem with random approximation space.
author: Giovanni Ballarin, Lyudmila Grigoryeva, Lukas Gonon

title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
summary: Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. A key advantage is its flexibility in the choice of source distribution, such as heavy-tailed and multimodal sources.
author: Yuchen Zhou, Lili Zheng, Yuxin Chen, et al.

title: Conformal Selection for Hierarchical Streaming Data
summary: Many real-world tasks involve making sequential decisions about whether to select candidates before their responses of interest are revealed. In this work, we address the online selection problem in the context of hierarchical data, where candidates arrive sequentially from different populations.
author: Zhenyuan Sun, Chengyao Yu, Ruixing Ming, et al.

title: A Statistical Framework for Training Data Auditing of Large Language Models
summary: Training-data auditing asks whether data of interest were used to train a large language model (LLM), a question central to privacy auditing, copyright protection, and benchmark-contamination detection.
author: Shengjie Niu, Yeheng Ge, Jian Huang

title: Time Series Structure Learning with Local Causal Parent Discovery
summary: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality.
author: Jacqueline Maasch, Shu Wan, Hank Zhu, et al.

title: Attention Head Specialization: Phase Transitions in Sample Complexity
summary: Attention heads specialize into distinct functions during training, often emerging in stages together with sharp changes in model behavior. While this phenomenon has mostly been studied as a function of training time, we ask how head specialization depends on the amount of available training data.
author: Léo Catteau, O. Duranthon, Lenka Zdeborová

title: Hellinger Decision Trees for Density Ratio Estimation: Finite-Sample Guarantees
summary: Density ratios play a central role in two-sample comparison, distribution-shift adaptation, and generative-model evaluation. However, estimating a density ratio through separate estimation of the underlying densities can be unnecessarily challenging.
author: Ren-Rui Liu, Zheng-Chu Guo

title: Closing Performance Gap for Diffusion Language Models under Low Inference Budgets
summary: Diffusion language models offer an architectural route to low-budget generation by updating multiple tokens in parallel, which can reduce the number of sequential decoding steps relative to token-by-token autoregressive decoding.
author: Hao Wu, Sipeng Chen, Jingwen Fu, et al.

title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
summary: Estimating the score function of a distribution plays a central role in statistics and machine learning, with applications in distribution estimation, sampling, and score-based generative modeling. However, learning scores from sensitive data raises privacy concerns.
author: Mengxiao Gao, Elly K. H. Hung, Yuchen Wu, et al.

title: Sequential Probability Assignment against Smoothed Adversaries with Unknown Base Measure
summary: Smoothed online learning has recently been studied as a way to bypass hardness results for the fully adversarial setting, which can be overly pessimistic. In this framework, the adversary is constrained to generate contexts from distributions having a bounded density with respect to some fixed base measure μ.
author: Ziyi Liu, Daniel M. Roy

title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to
summary: Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development.
author: Yin Liu, Shanshan Zhao, Didong Li

title: Instance-Optimal Moment Estimation in the Add-Remove Model of Differential Privacy
summary: In this paper, we study the problem of estimating empirical means, variances, and covariances under pure differential privacy in the add-remove model. While existing mechanisms achieve optimal worst-case error, they may not be optimal for individual datasets.
author: Shokichi Takakura

title: Causal Discovery with False Positive Error Control
summary: Causal discovery methods produce data-driven hypotheses about causal relationships, which may become new scientific findings or inform decisions about downstream interventions. In such settings, false positive causal claims can be more consequential than false negatives.
author: Erik Jahn, Venkat Chandrasekaran, Frederick Eberhardt, et al.

title: Fundamentals for Binary Classification Under Label Noise
summary: This chapter surveys fundamental results for binary classification under label noise. Binary classification under label noise involves training models on datasets where class labels are partially incorrect, leading to degraded performance and misclassification.

title: Prescribed Bayesian Efficiency under Lifetime Adjustment Costs

summary: We study the computational limits of clustering n observations drawn from a mixture of K isotropic Gaussian distributions in \mathbb R^d, when the number K of groups is much larger than the dimension d. In this regime, distance-based and spectral procedures require a squared separation Δ^2 of order \sqrt d.
author: Alexandra Carpentier, Nicolas Verzelen

title: HapBO: Harnessed α-π Bayesian Optimization via Expert Natural Language Priors

title: Empirical Variational Bayes Factorization for Longitudinal Matrix Data
summary: Collecting high-dimensional data over time for multiple individuals is increasingly common in biomedical research, particularly in studies of disease progression or molecular time-course experiments. Often data are missing or the timepoints are irregularly spaced across individuals.

summary: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. summary: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization.
author: Samet Demir, Zafer Dogan

title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators
summary: We present a general framework for modeling and learning equivariant functions between finite dimensional semisimple real group representations, unifying constructions developed across many application areas.

title: Path-Independent Deleveraging Rules
summary: We characterise path-independent auto-deleveraging (ADL) rules as an extended log-exponential family. Immunity to account splitting, merging and reopening further restrict the class. Homogeneity (essentially) restricts the class to a one-parameter family ordered by both fairness and platform risk.
author: Christoph Schlegel, Akaki Mamageishvili

title: Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility
summary: We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility U(x)=-x^{-γ}, γ>0. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control.

title: Bond yield dynamics: a multi-country multi-horizon string model
summary: This article extends the forward rate curve model of Baaquie and Bouchaud (2004) and Le Coz and Bouchaud (2024) to the multi-country setting of government bond markets. Cross-country blocks of correlation matrices of realized yield changes are found to display significant asymmetry between maturities.

title: A Three-Factor Hull-White Scenario Generator for Macro-Financial Stress Forecasting
summary: This paper builds a scenario engine that maps a yield-curve path into a distribution of macro-financial outcomes. A three-factor Hull-White model generates arbitrage-free curves whose factors are simulated under the physical measure, with an estimated and reported market price of risk.

title: Equity and Aggregate Ambiguity
summary: Equitable resource allocations in the context of symmetric risk exposures are intuitively desirable and sometimes even expected in public planning. However, public planners generally are also concerned with mitigating risk and, more generally, uncertainty and ambiguity.
author: Jose Blanchet, Yang Liu, Tiantian Mao, et al.

summary: This paper asks whether stablecoin runs carry information about U.S. Treasury yields. summary: We construct sub-replicating portfolios of vanilla options for a basket call when the marginal distributions of the underlying assets are known and their dependence is not. title: Neckpinches in a Positively Curved Market: Ricci Flow with Surgery on the Nikkei-225
summary: We study the intrinsic geometry of the Nikkei-225 through the discrete Ollivier-Ricci curvature (ORC) of its empirical correlation graph, using the graph Ricci flow and surgery methodology of arXiv:2510.15942.
author: Siddharta Laloux, Bhargavi Srinivasan

summary: An institution must complete a portfolio adjustment, but traders who prepare inventory for it can choose whether to participate. We study how public forecasts affect the institution's cost in a Bayesian execution game with optional activation, transient impact, and uniform-price terminal completion.
author: Khizar Qureshi

title: Auto-Alpha: A Framework for Autonomous Factor Research
summary: Autonomous factor research requires generating economic hypotheses as well as implementing and testing them. We present Auto-Alpha, a framework that connects report-guided initialization to self-directed research through a test-driven implementation loop.
author: Hui Cai, Kangcheng Deng, Tianyi Ma, et al.

title: The Coevolution and Coexistence of Humans and AI
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems replicate through deployment, vary through training, and compete for computational resources. These processes create the conditions for natural selection and raise a fundamental question: will AI evolve to benefit the humans on whom it depends?
author: Andrew W. Lo, Chaoyi Zhao

title: Quantum Calibration of Local-Volatility Surfaces from Sparse Option Quotes
summary: Calibrating a volatility surface from sparse option prices requires repeated solutions of a pricing equation as the volatility parameters change. We implement a hybrid quantum and classical method for this inverse problem using the Dupire local-volatility model.

summary: Options on VXX bring the dynamics of the VIX futures curve into the joint SPX-VIX calibration problem. summary: We prove that the equilibrium state-price deflated cum-dividend stock-price process in Guasoni, Larsen, and Leoni (2025) is a strict local martingale. Our result is based on proving that the unrestricted trader faces an endogenously complete model.

title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
summary: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Yet most are built around relatively static workflows and struggle to preserve reliable state as the environment changes.
author: Haozhe Wu, Zhonghang Li, Chao Huang

title: ChainIT Transaction Truth: Stablecoins, Web3 Wallets, and Multi-Rail Commerce. A Zero-Trust
summary: Stablecoins can move value continuously across programmable networks, and Web3 wallets can authorize those transfers with cryptographic signatures, but neither capability, standing alone, establishes a complete commercial transaction.
author: Eric Tacl, Matthew Koepp, Tim Hines, et al.

title: Sensitivity analysis in real options studies: systematic review and recommendations
summary: Real options (RO) modeling provides a powerful framework for valuing managerial flexibility under uncertainty in capital-intensive investments across various industries, including climate, energy, and transportation. However, the transparency and usefulness of such models depends heavily on sensitivity analysis (SA).
author: Mariia Kozlova, Julian Scott Yeomans

title: Algorithmic Market Making Can Lead to Rough Volatility Through the Order Book
summary: Existing work suggests that markets can show volatility with paths rougher than those of Brownian motion. In theory this can happen when the order flow is close to instability with memory that decays as a power law.
author: Sai Niranjan Ramachandran

title: When Price Charts Rhyme: Historical Visual Retrieval for Stock Return Prediction
summary: We study whether visually similar price histories predict similar future returns, using a vision model to retrieve each stock's most similar charts from three decades of U.S. price histories.
author: Hui Chen, Haoyu Liu, Ke Wu, et al.

summary: We price corridor products under a N-layered local volatility, piecewise constant in the price and in time, with knock-out barriers. A spatial scale transformation and the GIT method reduce the killed Green's function to a symmetric tridiagonal system of fixed size N-1.
author: Andrey Itkin, Dmitry Muravey

title: Total Positivity Properties of American Options
summary: Call option prices, viewed as functions of strike and time-to-expiration, are totally positive of order 2 (TP2) if the ratio of the price of a higher-strike call to a lower-strike call increases with time-to-expiration. A corresponding property applies to put option prices.
author: Paul Glasserman, Mike Li, Dan Pirjol

title: Which Past Matters? Training History and Multi-Forecast Horizon in Equity Transformers
summary: More historical data can improve estimation while introducing relationships that transfer poorly to current market conditions. We therefore examine how training quantity and historical selection interact with forecast horizon in intraday equity prediction.
author: Chariton Chalvatzis

summary: Differentiable programming enables online calibration of numerical models by minimizing errors accumulated along simulated trajectories. This includes estimating physical parameters and training neural sub-models in hybrid configurations.

title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part I: physical-space structures
summary: Vertically resolved budget analyses of frozen moist static energy (FMSE) variance within a cloud-resolving model provide a rigorous perspective on the equilibrium state of deep convective self-aggregation.
author: Lorenzo Silvestri, Paolina Bongioannini Cerlini, Andrea Cimarelli

title: Solving the puzzle of tropical cyclone track bifurcation
summary: Tropical cyclones whose predicted tracks bifurcate are among the most dreaded storms in disaster planning. Understanding when and why these bifurcations occur has been a long-standing puzzle in track forecasting. We address this issue by introducing the concept of "fate boundaries" hidden in the steering flow.

summary: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement; an autonomous agent cannot be assumed to supply it.
author: Ivan Kuznetsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin, Sonja Hänzelmann, et al.

title: Evaluation of machine-learning and deep-learning SPEI drought forecasts against persistence
summary: Bangladesh, home to nearly 178 million people, is highly vulnerable to recurring droughts that threaten food security and rural livelihoods. Machine-learning and deep-learning models are increasingly used to forecast drought indices such as the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI).
author: Mahir Ahnaf, Showmitra Kumar Sarkar

title: Where hurricanes get their spin: angular momentum versus kinetic energy
summary: Tropical cyclones almost never form within a few degrees of the equator. Their energy source, the heat engine fueled by the warm ocean, is available there as everywhere else. What is missing must be the other ingredient a cyclone needs, absolute angular momentum about the local vertical.
author: Boris Galperin, Jun A. Zhang

title: Vertical Structure-Based Composites for Analyzing Atmospheric Front Environments
summary: In many mid-latitude regions, a substantial fraction of extreme precipitation events occur in the vicinity of atmospheric fronts. To understand the processes that lead to such extreme precipitation, it is important to study the environment of the front.
